name: powerMouseV1
setupFrom: its README (npm install, edit config.json, npm start)

install.lockfile: bench/contenders/powermouse-v1/package-lock.json (what `npm install` resolved for its package.json ranges on 2026-11-11; the repo has none), copied into the clone
install.node: ctx.node (Node 24 in the measured runs; the README says Node 14)

run.command: node app.js (`npm start`), a copy of app.js in a run directory that is the process's working directory
run.runDir: <contenders>/powermouse-v1/.bench-run/<port>/ (config.json, urlData.json, and symlinks to ssl/, server.js, urlManager.js)
run.envNote: PORT would override config.json's port (its Heroku support)

appPatch.why: it proxies only hosts whose last label is on the public suffix list it downloads at start; .test (the fixture origins *.bench.test) is not on it, so the copy of app.js adds that one suffix; real sites see the list unchanged

hostnameNote: host page and proxy are addressed as localhost: on 127.0.0.1 the proxy derives a cookie Domain of ".0.0.1:<port>" from the Host header, which today's `cookie` package rejects, so every response is a 500

serve.proxy: its own server on a free port (http://localhost:<port>/)
serve./bench-config.js: generated by the adapter from this file (proxyOrigin)

navigation.homeNote: the host page opens the proxy home page first (sets its session cookie) and reports ready on its load
navigation.page: <proxy origin>/<absolute URL>, what its home page form (POST /prox) redirects to

transport.name: its own server
transport.summary: its own server: a Node {node} process fetches every page with node-fetch 2 (keep-alive agents, HTTP/1.1, redirects followed server-side) and returns it regex-rewritten; nothing goes through holyWisp

notes: server-side proxy: its fetches leave from Node, not through holyWisp (HTTP/1.1 only, Node TLS fingerprint, certificate checks off as in its code); DNS through the system resolver, with *.bench.test mapped to 127.0.0.1 by the harness shim
runs on Node {node}: no older Node needed (README says Node 14)

dependencies: the repo has no lockfile; what `npm install` resolves for its package.json ranges on 2026-11-11 is pinned by bench/contenders/powermouse-v1/package-lock.json (express 4.22, node-fetch 2.7, ws 7.5), installed with npm ci --ignore-scripts (no package has install scripts)

config.json as in the tree (directIPs false, ssl false, workers false: one worker thread) except listenip 127.0.0.1 and the port, written to a private copy in the run directory (README step 5 says to edit this file)

host page and proxy are addressed as localhost (the README says 127.0.0.1): on 127.0.0.1 its cookie Domain becomes ".0.0.1:<port>", which the current cookie package rejects, failing every request with a 500; on localhost the cookie is host-only
the proxy listens on its own port; the host page (another port, same site) frames it

the host page opens the proxy home page first (sets its session cookie, as a user visiting it does), then navigates the frame to <origin>/<url>, the URL its /prox form redirects to (one redirect saved)

at startup it fetches its public IP (api.ipify.org) and the public suffix list (publicsuffix.org); hosts whose TLD is not a public suffix get its "Bad domain" 404 page without being fetched; the harness runs a copy of app.js that appends "test" to that list, so the *.bench.test fixture origins load (the only change to its code)
it rewrites every page title to U+202E (by design) and strips integrity/nonce attributes; no service worker, no JavaScript API hooks beyond its 2 injected scripts
